title.ko: 관계·소통 구동사 get on · fall out · call off · find out
title.en: phrasal verbs for relationships and communication

explain.ko: 사람 사이의 관계와 의사소통을 말하는 구동사는 일상 대화에서 자주 쓰입니다. get on (well) with는 '~와 잘 지내다', fall out (with)은 '~와 사이가 틀어지다', make up은 '화해하다', run into는 '우연히 만나다', find out은 '알아내다', call off는 '취소하다', let down은 '실망시키다', look up to는 '존경하다'입니다. 분리형(call off, let down, find out)은 대명사를 가운데에 둡니다(call it off, let her down). 분리 불가형(get on with, run into, look up to)은 목적어를 뒤에 둡니다.
explain.en: Phrasal verbs for relationships and communication are very common in everyday speech: get on (well) with = have a good relationship; fall out (with) = quarrel; make up = become friends again; run into = meet by chance; find out = discover; call off = cancel; let down = disappoint; look up to = respect. Separable ones (call off, let down, find out) take a pronoun in the middle (call it off, let her down); inseparable ones (get on with, run into, look up to) keep the object after the particle.

notes.ko: get on with는 '진행하다'라는 뜻도 있어 문맥에 따라 달라집니다(Get on with your work!).
notes.en: Get on with also means continue (Get on with your work!); check the context.

notes.ko: call off는 수동태로 자주 씁니다(was called off).
notes.en: Call off is often used in the passive (was called off).

notes.ko: keep in touch는 구동사가 아니라 관용구로 전치사 with와 함께 씁니다.
notes.en: Keep in touch is an idiom; add with to name the person.

prompt.ko: 친구나 동료와의 관계에 대해 구동사를 사용해 4문장으로 써 보세요.
prompt.en: Write 4 sentences about your relationship with a friend or colleague, using phrasal verbs.

task.model: I get on well with my new colleagues. I keep in touch with my old friends after graduating. Yesterday I ran into an old friend at the market. She's someone I look up to. We fell out once, but we made up, and the meeting we planned was called off.

model_trans.ko: 나는 새 동료들과 잘 지내요. 졸업 후에도 옛 친구들과 계속 연락하고 있어요. 어제는 시장에서 오랜 친구를 우연히 만났어요. 그녀는 내가 존경하는 사람이에요. 우리는 한 번 사이가 틀어졌지만 화해했고, 계획했던 모임은 취소되었어요.
model_trans.en: I get on well with my new colleagues. I keep in touch with my old friends after graduating. Yesterday I ran into an old friend at the market. She's someone I look up to. We fell out once, but we made up, and the meeting we planned was called off.
